reason: Both starters own elite recent form — Rodriguez at a 2.76 xERA over his last 3 and Lambert at 2.65 xERA over his last 3 — and each faces a punchless lineup: HOU is a 68 wRC+ vs RHP over its last 6 (75 over its last 12) and LAA a 94 wRC+ vs RHP over its last 6 (83 over its last 12). Both bullpens back it up, HOU at 3.06 xERA and LAA at 2.58 xERA over their last 12. Two elite arms against two poor offenses with quality relief behind them does not support a 8.5, and the market has this priced as an average run environment.

HOU whiffs at a 23.5 K% vs RHP over its last 6, and he got 6 per start across two meetings with them. The line sits well below his recent output, and even a short leash does not threaten it given how many he misses per inning.

MIL makes plenty of contact at a 21.8 K% vs RHP over its last 6 with a 53.1 HH%, so there is no whiff spike coming. A line of 4.5 nearly doubles his recent per-start total, and getting plus money on the under is a clear mispricing.

Gasser has held up at home with a 3.55 ERA over his last 3 there and MIL has won its last 5 home starts behind him, while SEA's road bats managed just 3.0 runs per game over their last 5 SP starts. At home with that relief edge, MIL is worth more than this near-coinflip price.
